record.title: Mistral previews durable Managed Agents with restart recovery and approval waits
record.summary: Mistral introduced Managed Agents and its Python Agents SDK in public preview on 5 November. The documented service stores sessions for deployed agents, supports background execution and approval waits, and says a worker crash resumes from its last completed model or tool call. Teams can run the same agent in-process, self-host the harness or deploy a Mistral-managed worker. The documentation lists defaults of 24 hours per session, four idle hours and one hour for an approval wait, with higher limits configurable. These are provider-described capabilities; no independent service test or production outcome was verified.

claims.label: DEMONSTRATED
claims.text: Mistral published Managed Agents documentation and marked the Agents SDK and managed service as public preview on 5 November 2026.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: Mistral’s documentation describes durable sessions that can continue after the client app exits, resume after a worker crash from the last completed model or tool call, and wait for approval while the app is closed. It states that default session limits are 24 hours total, 4 hours idle, and one hour for an approval wait; higher session limits can be configured.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: Mistral documents a Python Agents SDK with three run modes: in-process development, self-hosted workers through agents serve, and Mistral-managed workers through agents deploy. In the deployed modes, Mistral stores session state; the harness and tool execution may run on the user’s servers or Mistral infrastructure.

claims.label: NOT_ESTABLISHED
claims.text: The announcement and documentation do not independently establish crash-recovery reliability, availability, isolation, security, production adoption, or improved agent task outcomes.

evidence_gaps.description: Durable resume, session persistence, approval timeout and worker behavior have not been independently exercised.
The preview documentation does not establish service availability, production reliability, workload limits beyond stated defaults or comparative operational cost.

brief.importance_rationale: If durable session recovery and approval waits work as documented, they change implementation choices for teams deploying long-running, tool-using agents by moving session persistence and orchestration into a shared SDK/service. This is a meaningful runtime design option; it does not establish reliability or better task outcomes.
limitations: Managed Agents and the SDK are explicitly in public preview, and their API, behavior and limits may change.
Crash recovery and approval-wait behavior are provider-documented but not independently tested here.
The documentation’s 24-hour total, 4-hour idle and one-hour approval-wait defaults can be raised; actual configured limits and account availability were not checked.
No independent evidence establishes security, uptime, customer adoption or improved task success.
brief.summary: Mistral introduced Managed Agents and its Python Agents SDK in public preview on 5 November. The documented service stores sessions for deployed agents, supports background execution and approval waits, and says a worker crash resumes from its last completed model or tool call. Teams can run the same agent in-process, self-host the harness or deploy a Mistral-managed worker. The documentation lists defaults of 24 hours per session, four idle hours and one hour for an approval wait, with higher limits configurable. These are provider-described capabilities; no independent service test or production outcome was verified.

technical.claimed_result: Mistral states that deployed agents can run for hours or days, continue when the client app exits, resume after a worker crash from the last completed model/tool call and wait for a person’s approval. The public-preview defaults are 24 hours per session, 4 idle hours and 1 hour awaiting approval; the documentation says limits can be raised.
technical.demonstrated_result: The official release note and documentation establish the dated public-preview announcement, published SDK/runtime description, deployment modes and default limits. They do not independently demonstrate runtime reliability.
technical.mechanism: The Agents SDK drives the model/tool loop and records steps in sessions. For deployed modes, Mistral stores session state separately from the client process. The harness can run on user-managed servers or as a Mistral-managed deployment; an optional per-session sandbox, approval gates, tracing and connectors are documented.
technical.regime: Python agent SDK and Studio deployment in public preview, announced 5 Nov 2026. Documentation describes in-process development, self-hosted agents serve and Mistral-managed agents deploy. Default session and approval timeouts are provider-documented; no account-specific settings or availability were tested.
technical.reproducibility: The public documentation provides setup examples and workflow description, but this review did not execute the SDK, inject crashes or verify state persistence and approval behavior.
technical.strongest_baseline: The provider documents in-process execution as the development mode: unlike deployed modes, its session lives in the application process and ends with it. No matched operational comparison was run.

brief.title: Mistral previews durable Managed Agents with restart recovery and approval waits
brief.why_it_matters: Long-running tool agents need durable state, recovery boundaries and human approvals that remain available when a client process stops. Mistral’s public-preview documentation describes these as runtime features of one SDK across self-hosted and hosted modes. If they work as specified, they could reduce custom orchestration work; reliability, security and task-level benefits still need independent testing.
